style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare-transliteration in amp with Strong's carried in notes (matching the ch.1 pilot); em-dashes used sparingly. Transliterations are ASCII-normalized (lowercase, diacritics dropped) relative to the lexicon's spellings.
chapterNote: With chapter 10 the book changes gear: the long fatherly lectures give way to the first great collection of stand-alone Solomonic proverbs, mostly two-line couplets set as sharp antitheses -- the righteous over against the wicked, the wise over against the fool, the diligent over against the sluggard. The dominant theme is the power of words: again and again the mouth, the lips, and the tongue are weighed, the righteous man's speech proving a fountain of life while the fool's chatter brings ruin. Running underneath is the book's deep conviction that the two ways do not merely differ in style but end in opposite places -- life or death, blessing or rot, a foundation that stands forever or a wickedness swept off like a passing storm.

1.text: The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish son is the heartache of his mother.
1.amp: The proverbs [mashal -- pithy sayings that set one thing beside another to teach] of Solomon. A wise [chakham -- skilled, discerning] son makes a father glad [samach -- rejoice], but a foolish [kesil -- dull, thick-headed] son is the grief [tugah -- sorrow, heaviness] of his mother.
1.notes: mashal (H4912) reopens the book's title, marking the start of the proverb collection proper. The verse pairs father and mother to show that a child's character lands on the whole household: chakham (H2450) gladdens, kesil (H3684) weighs the mother down with tugah (H8424), a heaviness of soul. Also tagged: samach (H8055).

2.text: Treasures gained by wickedness turn no profit at all, but righteousness rescues from death.
2.amp: Treasures [otsar -- stored-up wealth] of wickedness [resha -- wrongdoing, moral evil] gain nothing [yaal -- avail, do good], but righteousness [tsedaqah -- right dealing, righteous deeds] delivers [natsal -- snatches away, rescues] from death [mavet].
2.notes: otsar (H214) is a storehouse of riches, but riches piled up by resha (H7562) cannot finally yaal (H3276), profit. The contrast is not wealth against poverty but two destinies: tsedaqah (H6666) does what no hoard can -- it natsal (H5337), pulls a man back from mavet (H4194). Cf. 11:4.

3.text: The LORD will not let the righteous go hungry, but the craving of the wicked He thrusts away.
3.amp: The LORD [YHWH] will not let the soul [nephesh -- life, appetite] of the righteous [tsaddiq] go hungry [raeb -- famish, starve], but the craving [havvah -- greedy desire, calamity] of the wicked [rasha] He shoves aside [hadaph -- thrust, push away].
3.notes: the nephesh (H5315) here is the hungering self -- God keeps the tsaddiq (H6662) from starving. havvah (H1942) is a slippery word meaning both greedy craving and the ruin it brings; the LORD hadaph (H1920), thrusts the wicked man's grasping desire away unsatisfied, so that his very wanting becomes his undoing. Also tagged: YHWH (H3068), raeb (H7456), rasha (H7563).

4.text: A slack hand makes a man poor, but the hand of the diligent brings wealth.
4.amp: A slack [remiyah -- lazy, also deceitful] hand [kaph -- palm] makes one poor [rush -- become destitute], but the hand of the diligent [charuts -- sharp, decisive, hardworking] makes rich [ashar].
4.notes: remiyah (H7423) carries a double edge -- it means both slackness and deceit, hinting that laziness is its own kind of fraud. Set against it is charuts (H2742), literally something 'sharpened' or 'cut decisively' -- the diligent hand is one that bites into the work. Poverty and wealth here follow from character, not chance. Also tagged: kaph (H3709), rush (H7326), ashar (H6238).

5.text: He who gathers in the summer is a prudent son, but he who sleeps through the harvest is a son who brings shame.
5.amp: He who gathers [agaph -- shuts in, closes away in store] in summer [qayits -- summer, the time of ripe fruit] is a prudent [sakal -- insightful, acting wisely] son, but he who sleeps [radam -- lie in heavy sleep] in harvest [qatsir] is a son who causes shame [bosh -- disgrace].
5.notes: qayits (H7019) and qatsir (H7105) name the narrow seasons when crops must be brought in -- miss the window and the year is lost. sakal (H7919) is wisdom that produces results; the sluggard who radam (H7290), sleeps heavily, through the one season that feeds the family becomes a living bosh (H954), a walking disgrace to his house. The gathering verb is agaph (H103), literally to shut or close -- the harvest brought in and shut up safe in the storehouse before the season turns.

6.text: Blessings crown the head of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
6.amp: Blessings [berakah] are on the head [rosh] of the righteous [tsaddiq], but violence [chamas -- brutal wrong, injustice] covers [kasah -- conceal] the mouth [peh] of the wicked [rasha].
6.notes: berakah (H1293) settles on the rosh (H7218) like a crown or an anointing. The second line is deliberately ambiguous: either the wicked man's mouth hides the chamas (H2555) he plots, or the violence he has done at last muzzles and covers him -- both senses ring true, and the verse will be echoed word-for-word in v.11. Also tagged: tsaddiq (H6662), kasah (H3680), peh (H6310), rasha (H7563).

7.text: The memory of the righteous is a blessing, but the name of the wicked rots away.
7.amp: The memory [zeker -- remembrance, the name kept alive] of the righteous [tsaddiq] is a blessing [berakah], but the name [shem -- name, reputation] of the wicked [rasha] rots [raqab -- decays, festers].
7.notes: in a culture where a man lived on through his remembered name, this is no small thing: the zeker (H2143) of the righteous becomes a berakah (H1293), spoken with gratitude by those who follow. The shem (H8034) of the wicked, by contrast, does not merely fade -- it raqab (H7537), it rots, the same word used of decaying flesh and worm-eaten wood. Also tagged: tsaddiq (H6662), rasha (H7563).

8.text: The wise in heart takes correction to himself, but the babbling fool comes crashing down.
8.amp: The wise [chakham] in heart [leb] receives [laqach -- takes, accepts] commandments [mitsvah], but a fool of lips [evil -- a moral fool] comes to ruin [labat -- is thrown down, beaten].
8.notes: the contrast is between intake and output: the chakham (H2450) of leb quietly laqach (H3947), takes in instruction, while the fool runs his mouth. 'Babbling fool' renders the Hebrew idiom 'a fool of lips' -- all talk, no listening -- and such a one is labat (H3832), tripped up and flattened by his own chatter. The same downfall recurs in v.10. Also tagged: leb (H3820), mitsvah (H4687), evil (H191).

9.text: He who walks in integrity walks secure, but he who twists his ways will be found out.
9.amp: He who walks [halak] in integrity [tom -- wholeness, blamelessness] walks securely [betach -- in safety, confidence], but he who makes his ways crooked [aqash -- bend, pervert] will be known [yada -- exposed, found out].
9.notes: tom (H8537) is the soundness of a life with no hidden seam (cf. 2:7); such a man walks betach (H983), in settled confidence, because he has nothing to hide. The one who aqash (H6140), twists his paths, may go undetected for a while, but he 'will be known' (yada, H3045) -- exposure is only a matter of time. Also tagged: halak (H1980).

10.text: He who winks the eye sows trouble, and the babbling fool comes crashing down.
10.amp: He who winks [qarats -- pinch, signal slyly] with the eye [ayin] gives [natan] sorrow [atstsebeth -- pain, grief], but a fool of lips [evil] comes to ruin [labat].
10.notes: the sly wink (qarats, H7169) is the gesture of the schemer who signals mischief to a confederate while wearing an innocent face; it natan (H5414), deals out, atstsebeth (H6094), hidden hurt to others. The second line repeats v.8's verdict on the loud-mouthed fool -- both the secret schemer and the open babbler end the same way, undone by their own mouths. Also tagged: ayin (H5869), evil (H191), labat (H3832).

11.text: The mouth of the righteous is a wellspring of life, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
11.amp: The mouth [peh] of the righteous [tsaddiq] is a fountain [maqor -- spring, source] of life [chay], but violence [chamas] covers [kasah] the mouth [peh] of the wicked [rasha].
11.notes: maqor (H4726) is a living spring that never runs dry -- the righteous man's words refresh and sustain all who drink from them. The second line repeats v.6 exactly, framing the contrast: speech either pours out life or hides chamas (H2555), and a man's mouth reveals which kind of well lies beneath. Cf. John 4:14. Also tagged: peh (H6310), tsaddiq (H6662), chay (H2416), kasah (H3680), rasha (H7563).

12.text: Hatred stirs up quarrels, but love throws its cover over every offense.
12.amp: Hatred [sinah] stirs up [ur -- rouse, awaken] strife [medan -- contention, quarrels], but love [ahavah] covers [kasah -- conceal, draw a cover over] all wrongs [pesha -- transgressions, rebellions].
12.notes: sinah (H8135) ur (H5782), wakes up and inflames every grievance into medan (H4090), open quarrel -- a by-form of the more common madon. ahavah (H160) does the opposite -- it kasah (H3680), covers, the very pesha (H6588) that hatred exposes. This is not concealing sin to excuse it but refusing to broadcast a brother's fault; James and Peter both draw on it (Jas 5:20; 1 Pet 4:8).

13.text: On the lips of the discerning, wisdom is found, but a rod is for the back of the senseless.
13.amp: On the lips [saphah] of him who has understanding [biyn -- discernment] wisdom [chokmah] is found [matsa], but a rod [shebet -- staff, rod of discipline] is for the back [gev] of him who lacks heart [chaser leb -- void of sense].
13.notes: biyn (H995) is the trained ability to tell things apart; on such a man's lips chokmah (H2451) is matsa (H4672), readily found. The fool is literally 'lacking heart' (leb, H3820, being the seat of sense, not feeling) -- and what wisdom guides in the discerning, the shebet (H7626) must beat into the senseless from outside. Cf. 26:3. Also tagged: saphah (H8193), gev (H1460), chaser (H2638).

14.text: The wise store up knowledge, but the mouth of the fool invites ruin close at hand.
14.amp: The wise [chakham] lay up [tsaphan -- hide away, treasure] knowledge [daat], but the mouth [peh] of the foolish [evil] is near [qarov -- close, imminent] ruin [mechittah -- destruction, terror].
14.notes: tsaphan (H6845) is the treasure-hiding verb of 2:1 -- the wise quietly stockpile daat (H1847) against the day of need. The fool stockpiles nothing; his unguarded peh keeps mechittah (H4288), sudden collapse, perpetually qarov (H7138), close at hand, because his reckless words are forever one sentence from disaster. Also tagged: chakham (H2450), peh (H6310), evil (H191).

15.text: The wealth of the rich is his fortified city; the ruin of the poor is their poverty.
15.amp: The rich man's [ashir] wealth [hon -- riches, substance] is his strong [oz -- strength, fortress] city [qiryah], but the ruin [mechittah] of the poor [dal -- weak, lowly] is their poverty [resh -- destitution].
15.notes: the proverb states a hard fact of the world rather than a moral ideal: hon (H1952) functions as a man's oz (H5797), his walled city of defense, while the dal (H1800), the helpless poor, have only their resh (H7389), their want, which leaves them exposed to every blow. Read with the whole book, it is sober observation -- riches give real protection, but a protection the next chapters will call deceptive (cf. 11:28; 18:11). Also tagged: ashir (H6223), qiryah (H7151), mechittah (H4288).

16.text: The wages of the righteous lead to life; the gain of the wicked leads to sin.
16.amp: The labor [peullah -- work, its wages] of the righteous [tsaddiq] tends to life [chay], but the gain [tevuah -- produce, income] of the wicked [rasha] to sin [chattath].
16.notes: peullah (H6468) is both the work and the pay it earns; the righteous man's earnings flow toward chay (H2416), fuller life. The wicked man's tevuah (H8393), his yield, flows the other way -- toward chattath (H2403), more sin -- because gain in unrighteous hands only finances more wrong. It is not what a man earns but where it leads him. Also tagged: tsaddiq (H6662), rasha (H7563).

17.text: He who holds to correction is on the path of life, but he who throws off reproof leads others astray.
17.amp: He who keeps [shamar -- guards, observes] instruction [musar -- corrective discipline] is on the way [orach] of life [chay], but he who forsakes [azab -- abandons] reproof [tokachat -- rebuke] goes astray [taah -- wanders, and leads astray].
17.notes: musar (H4148) is the formative correction of 1:2-3; to shamar (H8104) it is to walk the orach (H734) of life. azab (H5800), to forsake it, is the abandoning-verb of 2:13, 2:17. taah (H8582) means to wander, and the older reading 'causeth to err' is apt -- the man who throws off reproof not only loses his own way but drags others off the road with him. Also tagged: chay (H2416), tokachat (H8433).

18.text: He who conceals his hatred has lying lips, and he who spreads slander is a fool.
18.amp: He who hides [kasah -- conceal] hatred [sinah] has lips [saphah] of falsehood [sheqer -- lie, deception], and he who spreads [yatsa -- bring out, put forth] slander [dibbah -- evil report] is a fool [kesil].
18.notes: two faces of the same malice: kasah (H3680) here is no longer love covering an offense (v.12) but hatred wearing a friendly mask, so the sheqer (H8267) is the smiling lie itself. Whether sinah (H8135) is hidden behind flattery or yatsa (H3318), broadcast as dibbah (H1681), open slander, the man who carries it is a kesil (H3684) -- both the quiet hypocrite and the loud gossip stand condemned. Also tagged: saphah (H8193).

19.text: Where words are many, sin is never far off, but he who holds his tongue is wise.
19.amp: In the abundance [rov -- multitude, the great many] of words [dabar] transgression [pesha -- rebellion, wrong] does not cease [chadal -- fail, stop], but he who restrains [chasak -- holds back, spares] his lips [saphah] is wise [sakal].
19.notes: rov (H7230) of dabar (H1697) -- a flood of talk -- makes pesha (H6588) all but inevitable; the more a man says, the more chance some of it is sin, so transgression 'does not chadal' (H2308), never lets up. Wisdom is shown not in fluency but in restraint: to chasak (H2820), to rein in the lips, is the act of the sakal (H7919), the truly prudent. Cf. Jas 1:19; 3:2. Also tagged: saphah (H8193).

20.text: Hand-picked silver -- that is what the righteous man's tongue yields; but weigh the inner self of the wicked, and it amounts to almost nothing.
20.amp: The tongue [lashon] of the righteous [tsaddiq] is choice [bachar -- selected, the best] silver [keseph], but the heart [leb] of the wicked [rasha] is of little [meat -- a small amount] worth.
20.notes: the proverb weighs words against worth: the tsaddiq's lashon (H3956) is keseph (H3701) bachar (H977), refined and hand-picked silver, valuable and pure. Against this whole treasure stands the rasha's leb (H3820), his inner self, which for all his scheming amounts to meat (H4592), next to nothing. What a man speaks is precious; what the wicked man is comes to almost nil. Also tagged: tsaddiq (H6662), rasha (H7563).

21.text: The lips of the righteous shepherd many, but fools die for want of sense.
21.amp: The lips [saphah] of the righteous [tsaddiq] feed [raah -- shepherd, pasture, nourish] many [rav -- the multitude], but fools [evil] die [muth] for lack [chaser] of sense [leb -- understanding].
21.notes: raah (H7462) is the shepherd's verb -- to lead a flock to pasture and feed it; the righteous man's words nourish rav (H7227), a whole crowd. The fool cannot even feed himself: he muth (H4191), dies, for lack of leb (H3820), the inner sense he refused to gain. The one gives life to many by speaking; the other loses his own for want of wisdom. Also tagged: saphah (H8193), tsaddiq (H6662), evil (H191), chaser (H2638).

22.text: It is the blessing of the LORD that makes a man rich, and He adds no sorrow with it.
22.amp: The blessing [berakah] of the LORD [YHWH], it makes rich [ashar], and He adds [yasaph -- increase, do again] no sorrow [etseb -- pain, toil] with it.
22.notes: berakah (H1293) from YHWH is set over against every fortune scraped together by toil and grasping. When God ashar (H6238), enriches, He does not yasaph (H3254), pile on, the etseb (H6089) -- the painful labor and grief -- that haunt wealth gotten any other way. The wording recalls the curse of Genesis 3:16-17; God's blessing reverses that ache rather than deepening it. Also tagged: YHWH (H3068).

23.text: Doing wickedness is sport to a fool, but wisdom is the delight of a man of understanding.
23.amp: It is as sport [sechok -- laughter, amusement] to a fool [kesil] to carry out [asah] mischief [zimmah -- evil scheme, depravity], but wisdom [chokmah] is the joy of a man of understanding [tebunah].
23.notes: the verse exposes what each man finds funny. To the kesil (H3684), working zimmah (H2154), a deliberate evil plan, is sechok (H7814), a game, a source of laughter. The man of tebunah (H8394) takes that same pleasure in chokmah (H2451) instead. A person's true character is laid bare by what amuses and satisfies him. Also tagged: asah (H6213).

24.text: What the wicked dreads will overtake him, but the longing of the righteous will be granted.
24.amp: The dread [megorah -- terror, the thing feared] of the wicked [rasha], it will come [bo -- arrive, overtake] upon him, but the desire [taavah -- longing] of the righteous [tsaddiq] He will grant [natan -- give].
24.notes: there is a grim symmetry here: the very megorah (H4034) the rasha tries to outrun will bo (H935), come upon him, while the taavah (H8378) the tsaddiq quietly hopes for, God will natan (H5414), give. Each man finally meets what his life is bent toward -- the wicked his nightmare, the righteous his hope. Cf. Job 3:25; Ps 145:19. Also tagged: rasha (H7563), tsaddiq (H6662).

25.text: When the storm has swept past, the wicked is gone, but the righteous stands on an everlasting foundation.
25.amp: As the whirlwind [suphah -- tempest, cyclone] passes [abar -- sweep over, pass by], the wicked [rasha] is no more, but the righteous [tsaddiq] is an everlasting [olam -- forever, perpetual] foundation [yesod -- base, footing].
25.notes: suphah (H5492) is the sudden, total storm that abar (H5674), roars through and is gone -- and the rasha is swept off with it, rootless. The tsaddiq is the opposite: a yesod (H3247), a laid foundation, that holds olam (H5769), forever. The image looks straight ahead to Christ's house built on rock, unmoved when the flood beats against it (Matt 7:24-27). Also tagged: rasha (H7563), tsaddiq (H6662).

26.text: Whoever sends the sluggard on an errand learns what he is -- a sourness that sets the teeth on edge, a sting of smoke that burns the eyes.
26.amp: As vinegar [chomets -- sour wine] to the teeth [shen] and as smoke [ashan] to the eyes [ayin], so is the sluggard [atsel -- the lazy one] to those who send [shalach -- dispatch on an errand] him.
26.notes: the proverb works by sensory disgust: chomets (H2558) sets the shen (H8127) on edge, ashan (H6227) stings the ayin -- two small, constant irritations. That is exactly what the atsel (H6102) is to the one who shalach (H7971), sends him on a task and waits, and waits: a low-grade exasperation that never delivers. Laziness is not just a private fault but a grief to everyone who depends on the lazy man. Also tagged: ayin (H5869).

27.text: Days upon days are added to the one who fears the LORD, but a wicked man's years are reaped off early.
27.amp: The fear [yirah -- reverent awe] of the LORD [YHWH] adds to [yasaph -- increases] one's days [yom], but the years [shanah] of the wicked [rasha] will be reaped off short [qatsar -- cut down, harvested].
27.notes: yirah (H3374) of YHWH -- the book's master theme (1:7) -- here yasaph (H3254), adds to, a man's yom (H3117), his span of days. The wicked man's shanah (H8141) are qatsar (H7114), cut short; the verb is a harvest word, 'to reap,' as if his life were a crop cut down before its time. The principle is general, the great pattern of how things tend, not a promise without exception. Also tagged: YHWH (H3068), rasha (H7563).

28.text: What the righteous wait for ripens into gladness; what the wicked count on perishes with them.
28.amp: The waiting hope [tochelet -- expectant waiting] of the righteous [tsaddiq] ripens into gladness [simchah -- joy], but the expectation [tiqvah -- hope, a stretched-out cord] of the wicked [rasha] will perish [abad -- be destroyed, vanish].
28.notes: tochelet (H8431) is hope that leans forward, waiting for what is sure; for the tsaddiq it resolves into simchah (H8057), settled joy. The rasha's tiqvah (H8615) -- a word picturing a taut cord of expectation -- simply abad (H6), snaps and perishes, the cord cut, the thing waited for never arriving. The two hopes look alike from the outside; only the end reveals the difference. Also tagged: tsaddiq (H6662), rasha (H7563).

29.text: The way of the LORD is a stronghold to the blameless, but ruin to those who work iniquity.
29.amp: The way [derek] of the LORD [YHWH] is strength [maoz -- fortress, refuge] to the upright [tom -- blameless], but destruction [mechittah] to the workers [paal -- those who do, fashion] of iniquity [aven -- wickedness, trouble].
29.notes: the same derek (H1870) of YHWH meets two men in opposite ways. To the man of tom (H8537), integrity, God's way is a maoz (H4581), a fortified refuge; to those who paal (H6466), actively manufacture, aven (H205), it is mechittah (H4288), their undoing. God Himself does not change -- the same righteousness that shelters the upright shatters the wicked. Cf. Luke 2:34; 2 Cor 2:15-16. Also tagged: YHWH (H3068).

30.text: The righteous will never be shaken loose, but the wicked will not go on dwelling in the land.
30.amp: The righteous [tsaddiq] will never [olam -- forever] be moved [mot -- totter, slip, be dislodged], but the wicked [rasha] will not dwell [shakan -- settle, abide] in the land [erets].
30.notes: mot (H4131) is the verb for tottering and slipping; the tsaddiq, olam (H5769), forever, will not be dislodged from his place (echoing the foundation of v.25). The rasha, by contrast, cannot shakan (H7931), take up lasting residence, in the erets (H776) -- the abiding, tabernacle-word for settled dwelling. To remain in the land is covenant blessing (cf. 2:21-22; Ps 37:29; Matt 5:5). Also tagged: tsaddiq (H6662), rasha (H7563).

31.text: The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom like fruit, but the twisted tongue will be cut out.
31.amp: The mouth [peh] of the righteous [tsaddiq] brings forth [nub -- bear fruit, flourish] wisdom [chokmah], but the perverse [tahpukot -- twisted, upside-down] tongue [lashon] will be cut off [karath -- severed].
31.notes: nub (H5107) is to bear fruit -- the righteous man's peh is a living tree that yields chokmah (H2451) in season. The tahpukot (H8419) tongue, the one that turns truth upside down, meets the orchard-keeper's pruning knife: it will be karath (H3772), cut off -- the same severe verb used for cutting off from the covenant people. Speech that bears no good fruit is finally lopped away. Also tagged: peh (H6310), tsaddiq (H6662), lashon (H3956).

32.text: The lips of the righteous know what wins favor, but the mouth of the wicked, only what is twisted.
32.amp: The lips [saphah] of the righteous [tsaddiq] know [yada -- discern, are practiced in] what is acceptable [ratson -- favor, what pleases], but the mouth [peh] of the wicked [rasha] speaks perversity [tahpukot -- twisted things].
32.notes: yada (H3045) here is more than information -- it is a trained instinct: the righteous saphah know by long practice what is ratson (H7522), fitting and welcome, both to God and to neighbor. The rasha's peh has the opposite reflex, pouring out tahpukot (H8419), the very twistedness of v.31. The chapter closes as it has run throughout, weighing the mouth and finding the whole man in it. Also tagged: saphah (H8193), tsaddiq (H6662), peh (H6310), rasha (H7563).
